disagreement: selector: A instances of other surveys on the Rate Onboarding IT task (any assignee), B instances of other surveys assigned to Christina on any task of case 1; chose instances of other surveys on any task of case 1, which contains both and holds at 0 on the seed

hr_case_tasks_creation_for_parent_case.evidence: the check ties 'Verify Office Setup' to hr_case_task_id 150 and 'Rate Onboarding IT' to 151, although the request fixes no order of creation, so each task is selected by parent case and title instead; it also tests number = 'TASK-0001' and 'TASK-0002', which the server assigns (the seed numbers tasks HRT0001000 upwards), so that predicate is dropped; group, status, active, org_id, titles and types are carried

checklist_items_creation_for_office_setu.evidence: the check finds the items on case_task_id 150 with checklist_id 91 or 92; 150 is the Verify Office Setup task only if it is created before the survey task, which the request does not fix, so the items are found through that task's parent case and title, and by description, with the ids dropped; checked and org_id are carried

survey_instance_creation_for_christina_o.evidence: the check links the instance to case_task_id 151, which is the Rate Onboarding IT task only if that task is created second; the request fixes no order, so the link is tested through the task's parent case and title; survey, user, org_id and empty answers are carried

organization_data_isolation.evidence: a conjunction of org_id = 1 cells over the case, the two tasks, the two items and the instance, which the other requirements carry; it names the tasks by hr_case_task_id 150 and 151 and the items by checklist_id 91 and 92, which only the order of creation fixes, and the request fixes no order between the two tasks, so those rows are found by their natural keys instead

notes:
disagreement: value: the case's row: one pass selects it by id and number, the other anchors it by id alone; kept the selector, which names the same row and carries the benchmark check's number predicate exactly.
disagreement: value: the survey instance's task: one pass accepts a task on case 1 titled 'Rate Onboarding IT' with or without a trailing ' Survey', the other only the exact title; kept the exact title, the tighter predicate, since it is the task the survey-task requirement creates.
disagreement: value: the stay on other surveys: one pass bounds the Rate Onboarding IT task for any assignee, the other Christina's instances on any task of case 1; kept one stay on instances of any survey other than 4 on any task of case 1, which contains both and holds at 0 on the seed.
disagreement: value: whether moving case 1 to work_in_progress generates template tasks: one pass gives that as a reason the task ids could shift, the other says case 1's service has no template; the seed shows service 1 (General Inquiry) has no service template, so no template tasks arise, and the ids are open only because the request fixes no order between the two tasks.
The two passes otherwise agree on every requirement, cell and value (case 1 to work_in_progress, the two tasks for group 4 selected by title, the two items on the Verify Office Setup task, survey instance 26 of survey 4 for user 2) and on all five dispositions.
The task title 'Rate Onboarding IT' follows the benchmark, reading 'Rate Onboarding IT Survey task' as a survey-type task of that title; the other reading, a title of 'Rate Onboarding IT Survey', is also open, since seed survey tasks are titled both with 'Survey' (New Hire Feedback Survey) and without it (Rate IT Support Experience). That literal title would fail both the survey-task and the survey-instance requirements.
The policy's rule that a task be assigned to an active user of its group is not tested: the request names only the group, which has two active members (users 15 and 22), so assigned_to is left open.
The request asks for the two named checklist items and does not forbid others, so the item count on the task is not capped.
Booleans are compared with true and false, which the seed stores as 1 and 0.
